newsitem.title: USA: Railroad board issues Conrail merger timetable.
newsitem.headline: Railroad board issues Conrail merger timetable.

text.p: Money aside, bids by two big eastern freight railroads to buy Conrail Inc. will ultimately be decided by the U.S. Surface Transportation Board, but not likely before early 1998.
And it could be later than that.

The board, which has replaced the defunct Interstate Commerce Commission as railroad regulator, said on Monday that Norfolk Southern Corp had submitted a notice that it would file an intent to buy Conrail by May 1.
Earlier, the other Conrail suitor, CSX Corp, said it intended to file its intent to acquire Conrail by March 1, board spokesman Dennis Watson said.
The board Friday issued its timetable for considering the acquisition, with its decision -- based on the national interest -- coming 300 days after the formal filing.
Watson said a formal decision on the CSX bid then might be issued in February 1998, but if the Norfolk Southern bid was being considered, the final order could slip to April 1998.
And further delays are possible pending court actions.

CSX and Norfolk Southern are locked in a bidding war for Philadelphia-based Conrail. CSX, of Richmond, Virginia, made the first bid for it. Its offer was followed shortly by one from Norfolk Southern, of Norfolk, Virginia.

Watson said if both CSX and Norfolk Southern filed to buy Conrail, the board would likely judge the bids simultaneously, with each side making its case and a decision issued based on what best serves the public.
The board issued this timetable for action:
- 30 days before formal filing - reports on environmental impact, as well as requests for line abandonment; line construction and terminal control;
- 30 days after filing - board's notice of acceptance of applications published in the Federal Register;
- 75 days - comments, protests, requests for conditions to be applied to the merger, and other opposition evidence;
- 90 days - comments by the Justice and Transportation Departments;
- 235 days - oral arguments before the board;
- 240 days - board holds open voting meeting;
- 300 days - board issues final written decision, reflecting its vote.
